intro: One person, a whole life. Drag the age marker from birth to 90 and watch four lanes change at once: how the person thinks (Piaget's stages, then adult intelligence), the question they are working through (Erikson's psychosocial stages), their relationships, and their body and roles from puberty to emerging adulthood. Then switch lenses to see a strange-situation reunion, set a parent's warmth and rules, and follow crystallized and fluid intelligence into old age.
howItWorks:
Every person and every study in this trainer is invented for practice. The stage ages are the usual textbook ages: real children reach milestones at different times, and later research found infants and preschoolers can do some things earlier than Piaget thought. The adult intelligence curves are a sketch of the well-known pattern, not data from one study. Freud's psychosexual stages are not part of the AP® Psychology course, so they are left out.

In Test yourself, each problem places a person on the lifespan. Name the stage or pattern first; the timeline lights up only after you answer, so the picture never gives the key away. Then apply it: the concept the behavior shows, the next crisis, or what the research can and cannot conclude.
